rows.description: A teenager tells different versions of themselves to different friends, often exaggerating. Story-telling to peers is partly an experiment in who they might be.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A person in therapy or in reflection retells a painful event with a focus on what they survived and learned. Redemptive retelling should be honest and not erase real harm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A young adult labelled as the difficult one or the lazy one in the family lives inside that story. Stepping out of an assigned role takes many small acts of behaving differently.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: Friends tease each other about a haircut and laugh together, both aware it is affectionate. The line is that everyone involved enjoys it and can say stop.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child laughs along at nicknames about their body while feeling ashamed. Not objecting does not mean not hurting, and children often fear being seen as too sensitive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, fear, shame, hurt

rows.description: A teenager pushes banter further to gain status, hitting soft spots such as weight, family or skin colour. Cruelty disguised as jokes is common, and it usually shows in the target's face.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager says that one is not okay in a calm voice, or changes the subject. Naming a boundary once, clearly, is stronger than laughing it off, and good friends adjust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: Someone realises a joke hurt and says I am sorry, that was not okay, without adding but you are too sensitive. A clean apology repairs trust faster than a defence of intent.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child avoids telling a parent about a low grade or a quarrel and delays until it grows. Avoidance makes the eventual talk harder, and a calm parent makes the first admission easier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager in a serious conversation with a parent feels heat, cannot think, and blurts or shuts down. When the body is flooded, pausing and resuming later works better than pushing through.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
